results.body: {subject} looks at you, then laughs for the first time on record. The following week you are asked to join something with a name. The delay is not raised again.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} nods gravely and says those values mean a great deal. You have made a sincere impression on someone you were trying to make laugh.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Tell {subject} that you could help look for a certain list

results.body: {subject} goes very still, then asks you for a word outside. From now on {subject} speaks well of you, to everyone, with a slight tremor.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} asks which list. You say it does not matter. It now does, and {subject} has mentioned it to the Office Co-ordinator.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Ask {subject} how things are looking at the competition

results.body: {subject} closes the laptop and looks at you properly for the first time. After the meeting {subject} offers you some advice, which is good, and asks you for your silence, which is free.
results.factNote: What you were told about {subject} was so, and you knew to use it.

results.body: {subject} says they are doing rather well, and sends you the market report. You have fifty pages to read and nothing to show for it.
results.factNote: You acted on something you were told about {subject}. It was not so.

options.label: Mention, modestly and twice, the long evenings you spent on the team's figures

results.body: You have seen how this is done, and you do it. The figures were mostly the Senior Analyst's, and so were the evenings, but the Senior Analyst is not asked. Your name moves up the curve by a small, well-lit amount.

news.text: You took the credit for the team's figures at Calibration.

verdict.warm: Afterwards your boss takes you aside, and says that you are one of the few people here who really gets it. Your boss does not say what it is. You are rated Meets, warmly, and your boss shakes your hand as if something had been agreed.
verdict.neutral: Afterwards your boss says that it has been a year, and that you were in it. You are rated Meets. Your boss holds the door for you, or possibly for the person behind you.
verdict.cold: Afterwards your boss says that the panel felt you had been on a journey, and that everyone is keen to see where you get off. You are rated Meets, with a note. Your boss signs the note, and spells your name with care, for the file.

title: The New Metric
narration: Your boss has introduced a new metric, the Stakeholder Delight Index. It will be reported monthly, and it goes up when a form is filled in. The first results are being shown today. Nobody has said who fills in the form.

signs.label: Whose number is not discussed
signs.text: Everyone's score goes up on the screen. {holder}'s is passed over with a nod, and {ignored}'s is left up there for some time.
signs.clue: At the metric review, {holder}'s number was passed over, and {ignored}'s was left on the screen.

signs.label: Who decides what it means
signs.text: {bystander} starts to say what the number shows, sees {holder}'s expression, and says what it shows instead.

options.label: Fill in the form yourself, on behalf of several stakeholders

results.body: Your Delight goes to ninety-four. Three stakeholders have now expressed delight, and one of them is a meeting room. You are asked to share your approach with the team.

options.label: Report the number you actually got

results.body: Your Delight is eleven. You say that this seems about right. There is a silence, and then someone asks whether eleven is out of eleven.

options.label: Ask the Senior Analyst, kindly, how their number was arrived at

results.body: The Senior Analyst answers at once, and thanks you, and looks at you for slightly too long. By the afternoon someone from upstairs has asked how your own number was arrived at.
results.factNote: You asked the Senior Analyst a tricky question. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: The Senior Analyst has to look it up. The room waits. You say that it is no problem at all, and that you were only curious, and everyone writes that down.

options.label: Say that this metric has really changed how you think

results.body: You say it with a straight face. Your boss says that this is exactly the sort of thing the metric was meant to do, though neither of you says what that is.

options.label: Look at the screen until it is over

results.body: It is over in forty minutes. You have been delighted, on the form, by somebody.

options.label: Catch your boss on the way out, and tell them you can get the team new laptops

results.body: You catch your boss at the door, and hear yourself say it.

title: Recruitment Panel
narration: The floor has a vacancy for an analyst, and you are on the panel, for balance. There are three candidates. One is excellent, one was recommended, and one is an old friend of yours who has asked you not to mention how you know each other.

signs.label: Whose candidate it is
signs.text: The panel goes round the table. Everyone looks at {holder} before giving a view, and {ignored} is thanked before finishing theirs.
signs.clue: On the Recruitment Panel, everyone looked at {holder} before giving a view, and {ignored} was thanked before finishing.

signs.label: Who has already decided
signs.text: {bystander} has filled in the scoring sheet in pen. {holder} has not filled in anything, and does not look as if that will matter.

options.label: Make the case for your old friend

results.body: Your friend gets the job, and takes you for a drink, and asks what the job is. You now have someone on the floor who owes you, and who cannot do anything.

news.text: You hired an old friend at the Recruitment Panel.

options.label: Argue for the excellent candidate

results.body: You go through the evidence, and they are appointed. They are very good. Everyone has already started to wonder what they are after.

news.text: You argued for the best person at the Recruitment Panel, and got them.

options.label: Say how impressed you were by whoever was recommended

results.body: You had not read the application. It does not come up. Your remarks are recorded as the view of the panel, which turns out to be the view of the person who made the recommendation.

options.label: Raise a concern about the Project Co-ordinator's preferred candidate

results.body: It seems to go well. Then you are asked, by someone from Human Resources you have never seen, to put your concern in writing, and to say how you came by it.
results.factNote: You raised a concern against the Project Co-ordinator's candidate. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: You do not say what the concern is. You say that you would just want to be sure. The candidate is thanked for their time, and the Project Co-ordinator thanks you for yours.

options.label: Tell the Project Co-ordinator that the next opening is as good as theirs

results.body: You say it by the coffee, afterwards, as though it were yours to say.

title: Speak Up Listening Session
narration: Human Resources is holding a Listening Session, in which anyone may raise anything in complete confidence, in this room, in front of everybody. There are biscuits. Someone from Human Resources is writing down who takes one.

signs.label: Who is safe to mention
signs.text: Several concerns are raised about the floor in general. Nobody's sentence ends anywhere near {holder}, and two of them end at {ignored}.
signs.clue: At the Listening Session, no concern came near {holder}, and two ended at {ignored}.

signs.label: Who is really listening
signs.text: The person from Human Resources writes down what {bystander} says, and then looks at {holder} to see whether to keep it.

options.label: Say what is actually wrong with your own project

results.body: You say it. It takes two minutes. The person from Human Resources thanks you for bringing your whole self to the session, and asks whether you would like to speak to someone.

options.label: Report your concerns about the Senior Analyst's expenses

results.body: You are thanked for your courage. A week later you are being asked about your own expenses, by name, going back to a sandwich in March.
results.factNote: You reported the Senior Analyst. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: You are thanked for your courage. The Senior Analyst has a brief, informal conversation, and comes back from it and sits down without looking at anyone. It is not known who said what, and everybody knows.

news.text: You reported the Senior Analyst's expenses at the Listening Session.

options.label: Mention, by the biscuits, that the Project Co-ordinator's project is in trouble

results.body: It gets round quickly. It gets round, in fact, to someone who knows where it started. You are sent a calendar invitation with no subject, and your boss is on it.
results.factNote: You started a rumour about the Project Co-ordinator. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: You say it to the Office Co-ordinator, by the biscuits, as something you had assumed everyone knew. By the time you reach your desk it has come back to you, with details. The Project Co-ordinator's project is in serious trouble, and people are being very kind about it.

falseStory.text: A story that the Project Co-ordinator's project was in trouble.

exposed.text: You started the story that the Project Co-ordinator's project was in trouble.

options.label: Say that you feel safe, and that you would like that recorded

results.body: It is recorded. You are asked whether you would be willing to say that on a poster. You find that you are.

options.label: Take the microphone, and say what you think of each of them, by name
options.stakes: It is being recorded. People have been walked out of the building for much less.

results.body: You are thorough. You use the word 'frankly' eleven times. The Listening Session is the first in the company's history to have listened, and the recording reaches the floor above before you have sat down.

options.label: Take a biscuit, and say nothing

results.body: It is a good biscuit. It has been noted.

title: Quarterly Business Review: The Pivot
location: The Auditorium, with every floor on the video link
narration: A new year's first Quarterly Business Review. Last year's arrow has been turned ninety degrees, and is now called a pivot. It points at a slide that says Beyond.

signs.label: Who names the pivot
signs.text: {holder} is asked what the pivot is towards, and says Beyond, and the room nods. {ignored} asks where Beyond is, and is thanked.
signs.clue: At the Pivot review, the room nodded when {holder} said Beyond, and thanked {ignored} for asking where it was.

signs.label: Who sits nearest
signs.text: {bystander} has saved the seat beside {holder}, and gives it up only when {holder} sits in it.

options.label: Say that your team pivoted first

results.body: You are minuted as an early pivoter. Nobody asks which way.

options.label: Ask where Beyond is, exactly

results.body: There is a pause. Someone says that is rather the point. Your question is noted, in a smaller font.

options.label: Thank your boss's boss for the vision

results.body: Your boss's boss accepts the thanks on behalf of the vision, which is not present.

options.label: Turn your chair ninety degrees, like everyone else

results.body: You face Beyond with the rest of the room. It is a wall.

title: Quarterly Business Review: Lessons From the Future
location: The Auditorium, with every floor on the video link
narration: This quarter's review looks back from next year, which has gone well. A consultant reads out what we will have learned, and the room takes notes on its own future.

signs.label: Whose future is read first
signs.text: The consultant reads out what {holder} will have achieved, at length. {ignored}'s future is in the appendix.
signs.clue: At the Lessons From the Future review, {holder}'s future came first and {ignored}'s was in the appendix.

signs.label: Who claps first
signs.text: {bystander} claps for a future achievement a moment after {holder} does, and a moment before anyone else.

options.label: Say that you will have delivered the new tool by then

results.body: It is written into next year, in your name. Next year has become a deadline.

options.label: Thank leadership for next year

results.body: Leadership thanks you for thanking them in advance. It is a first, and it is minuted.

options.label: Ask what we learned this year

results.body: The consultant says that this year is out of scope. It is in next year's lessons, as a risk.

options.label: Take notes on your future

results.body: Your notes say that things went well. You underline it.

title: Quarterly Business Review: The Year, Again
location: The Auditorium, with every floor on the video link
narration: The last review of the period. The slides are last year's, with the year changed, because the slides went well last year. The arrow is back, and is going up again, from where it was.

signs.label: Who notices the slides
signs.text: {holder} says that the slides look familiar, and everyone agrees that this is a strength. {ignored} says the same thing, and is asked to take it offline.
signs.clue: At the last review, the room agreed with {holder} that the slides looked familiar, and asked {ignored} to take it offline.

signs.label: Who speaks last
signs.text: {bystander} finishes a sentence only once {holder} has nodded at the end of it.

options.label: Present last year's slide as this year's

results.body: Nobody notices. Someone says it is even better than last year's, which it is not, being the same one.

options.label: Say that it is the same slide

results.body: There is a silence. The slide is advanced, and the next one is also the same.

options.label: Say that the arrow is all down to your boss

results.body: It is minuted, as it was last year, in the same words.

options.label: Nod at the arrow

results.body: You nod at the arrow. It is going up, and so, for a moment, are you.

title: The Stand-Up
narration: The daily stand-up, which is now monthly, and seated, and an hour. Everyone says what they did, what they will do, and what is blocking them, which is the stand-up.

signs.label: Who goes first
signs.text: {holder} is asked to go first, and says they will go last. Everyone waits for them anyway.
signs.clue: At the stand-up, everyone waited for {holder}, who had said they would go last.

signs.label: Who is cut short
signs.text: {ignored} is thanked halfway through a sentence, and the meeting moves on.

options.label: Say what you actually did

results.body: You say what you did. It takes eleven seconds, and someone asks whether that is everything.

options.label: Say that you are blocked by another team

results.body: You are blocked by another team. The other team is not here, and is minuted as a dependency.

options.label: Say that the stand-up keeps everyone aligned

results.body: Your boss agrees. The stand-up is extended by half an hour, so that it can keep everyone more aligned.

options.label: Stand up

results.body: You stand up. It is a stand-up. Nobody else does, and you sit down again.

title: Away Day Planning
narration: A meeting to plan the team's away day, which will be held in this room, to save money. There will be an icebreaker. There is already an ice.

signs.label: Who chooses the icebreaker
signs.text: {holder}'s icebreaker is chosen before the others are read out. {ignored}'s is the one about two truths and a lie.
signs.clue: At Away Day Planning, {holder}'s icebreaker was chosen before anyone else's was read.

signs.label: Who books the room
signs.text: {bystander} offers to book the room, and checks with {holder} first.

options.label: Offer to organise it all

results.body: You are organising the away day. It is in this room, so the logistics are mostly chairs.

options.label: Suggest spending the day on the actual work

results.body: There is a silence. Your boss says that is what the other days are for, and writes AGILITY on the whiteboard.

options.label: Suggest bringing in a facilitator

results.body: A facilitator is booked. Their fee is the away day's budget, so the away day is the facilitator.

options.label: Say you will bring biscuits

results.body: You are minuted as Biscuits. It is the clearest action on the page.

title: Process Improvement Review
narration: A review of the process for improving processes. The process has a flowchart, and the flowchart has a box that says Improve, with an arrow back to the start.

signs.label: Who owns the flowchart
signs.text: {holder} is asked whether the flowchart is right, and says that it is, and it is.
signs.clue: At the Process Improvement Review, {holder} said the flowchart was right, and that settled it.

signs.label: Whose box is removed
signs.text: {ignored}'s box is taken off the flowchart to simplify it. Nothing else changes.

options.label: Add a box called Review the Review

results.body: Your box is added. The flowchart is now longer, which is minuted as maturity.

options.label: Point out a step that nobody does

results.body: Everyone agrees that nobody does it. It is kept, so that it can be not done properly.

options.label: Say that you have never seen a clearer flowchart

results.body: Your boss says it took a lot of work. It took a lot of boxes.

options.label: Follow the arrow with your finger

results.body: Your finger goes round twice and comes back to the start. You are minuted as engaged.

title: Leadership Induction
narration: Your induction as a leader. Your boss welcomes you, and announces the Grand Plan, {plan}. Nobody says what it will excel at. There are pastries.

signs.label: Who takes the last pastry
signs.text: {holder} takes the last pastry without asking, and nobody minds. {ignored} had been looking at it.
signs.clue: At your Leadership Induction, {holder} took the last pastry, and nobody minded.

signs.label: Who explains the Plan
signs.text: {bystander} explains the Plan to you while looking at {holder}.

options.label: Ask what it will excel at

results.body: There is a pause. Your boss says that is what the Centre is for. Your question is written on a flipchart, under Parked.

options.label: Sign the leadership charter first

results.body: Your signature is the first on the charter, above where your boss's will go. It is moved down.

options.label: Take a pastry

results.body: It is a pain au chocolat. You are a leader now.

options.label: Say that you are humbled

results.body: You say it. Everyone who has said it before nods, humbly.

title: Team Leads' Sync
narration: The team leads' weekly sync, held monthly. Every team is at capacity.

signs.label: Whose capacity counts
signs.text: {holder}'s team being at capacity is minuted. {ignored} is asked for evidence.
signs.clue: At the Team Leads' Sync, {holder}'s word on capacity was minuted, and {ignored} was asked for evidence.

signs.label: Who sets the agenda
signs.text: {bystander} reads out the agenda, which {holder} sent round an hour ago.

options.label: Lend one of your team to another lead

results.body: One of your team is lent to the Service Delivery Lead for a month. They are told this by the Service Delivery Lead.

remembers.text: You lent them one of your team at the Team Leads' Sync.

options.label: Say that your team is at capacity

results.body: You say it. It is minuted. Your team is now officially at capacity, which means it can do less.

options.label: Staff the Centre of Excellence with your best people

results.body: Your best people move to the Centre. It has a desk now, and the desk has work on it.

options.label: Put a Centre of Excellence sign on an empty office

results.body: The sign is laminated. The office behind it has a chair, and the chair has a box of old cables on it.

options.label: Say that your team would not be at capacity, but for the Senior Analyst

results.body: It is minuted. That afternoon someone from upstairs asks, very politely, to see your own capacity, and who signed it off.
results.factNote: You blamed the Senior Analyst for your team's capacity at the Team Leads' Sync. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: It is minuted. The Senior Analyst reads the minutes, and replies to everyone that they have been carrying the team, with figures.

title: Resourcing Call
narration: A call about resourcing, which is a word for people. Your own team is on it, so that it can hear itself resourced. Some of them wanted your job.

signs.label: Who speaks for the team
signs.text: {holder} answers a question that was put to you, and nobody corrects it.
signs.clue: On the Resourcing Call, {holder} answered a question put to you, and nobody corrected it.

signs.label: Who is moved
signs.text: {ignored} is moved to another project in the course of a sentence, and finds out at the end of it.

options.label: Say that your team needs more people, not fewer

results.body: You say it. You are thanked for your advocacy, and your team is reduced by one, for balance.

options.label: Offer to do more with less

results.body: Your boss writes MORE WITH LESS on the whiteboard. Your team will be told by the whiteboard.

options.label: Report the Centre of Excellence as open for business

results.body: It is minuted as open. Business is welcome, by appointment, which nobody has.

options.label: Stay on mute

results.body: You stay on mute. Your team watches you stay on mute.

title: Leads' Huddle
narration: A huddle, which is a meeting that stands up so as to seem shorter. It is not shorter.

signs.label: Who ends it
signs.text: The huddle ends when {holder} sits down. Nobody had said it would.
signs.clue: At a Leads' Huddle, it ended when {holder} sat down.

signs.label: Who is not in the circle
signs.text: {ignored} stands slightly outside the circle, and is asked to speak up.

options.label: Share a win from your team

results.body: You share a win. Your boss asks whether it can be a case study. It is now a case study, and nobody on your team was asked.

options.label: Share a problem from your team

results.body: You share a problem. Your boss says it is good that we can be open, and changes the subject.

options.label: Move real work into the Centre of Excellence

results.body: Real work moves into the Centre. It is quieter there, and people get on with it.

options.label: Nod along

results.body: You nod. Huddles run on nodding.

title: Risk Register Review
narration: The risk register is reviewed. It has ninety risks, eight of them red. Each is owned by someone who is not in the room.

signs.label: Whose risks go amber
signs.text: {holder}'s red risks are agreed to be amber, on reflection. {ignored}'s amber risk is made red.
signs.clue: At the Risk Register Review, {holder}'s red risks became amber, and {ignored}'s became red.

signs.label: Who keeps the register
signs.text: {bystander} has the spreadsheet, and changes nothing until {holder} has spoken.

options.label: Take ownership of a red risk

results.body: The risk is yours. It is still red, and now it has your name on it.

options.label: Suggest that your red risk is really amber

results.body: It is amber now. Nothing about it has changed, except the colour.

options.label: List the Centre of Excellence as a mitigation for everything

results.body: The Centre mitigates thirty risks. It does not yet have anyone in it.

options.label: Assign the reddest risk to the Project Co-ordinator, who is not in the room

results.body: The risk is reassigned. By the morning it has been reassigned back to you, by someone from upstairs you have never met, with a note asking how you came to choose.
results.factNote: You gave the Project Co-ordinator the reddest risk on the register. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: The Project Co-ordinator finds out from the register, and thanks you for the development opportunity, in a reply all.

options.label: Read all ninety

results.body: You read all ninety. The fourth one is the risk that nobody reads the register.

title: Planning Pre-Meet
narration: A meeting before the planning meeting, to agree what the planning meeting will decide. The planning meeting has been told it is empowered.

signs.label: Who decides first
signs.text: {holder} says what the planning meeting will decide, and it is written down as a proposal.
signs.clue: At the Planning Pre-Meet, {holder} said what would be decided, and it was minuted as a proposal.

signs.label: Who is told afterwards
signs.text: {ignored} asks what was agreed, and is told that it will be agreed at the planning meeting.

options.label: Agree with whatever is going to be decided

results.body: You agree in advance. It saves time later, when you will agree again.

options.label: Propose something your team could actually do

results.body: It is minuted as an option. Options are what the planning meeting does not choose.

options.label: Suggest a pre-meet for the pre-meet

results.body: It is booked for Thursday. You will chair it, and it will decide what this one decided.

options.label: Offer to take the minutes

results.body: You take the minutes. They record that things were agreed.

title: The Retrospective
narration: A retrospective, on what went well and what did not. The one action is to hold another.

signs.label: Whose sticky note stays up
signs.text: {holder}'s note under What Went Well stays up. {ignored}'s falls off, and stays off.
signs.clue: At the Retrospective, {holder}'s note stayed up, and {ignored}'s fell off and stayed down.

signs.label: Who reads them out
signs.text: {bystander} reads the notes aloud, and pauses at {holder}'s.

options.label: Say what actually went wrong

results.body: You say it. It is written under What Did Not Go Well, in a smaller pen.

options.label: Say that everything went well

results.body: Everyone agrees, with relief. The retrospective ends early, which is minuted as a success.

options.label: Say that the process let everyone down

results.body: The process is blamed, unanimously. It is not present, and takes it well.

options.label: Tell the Senior Analyst by the kettle that your boss is on the way out

results.body: You tell the Senior Analyst, as something everyone already knows. By the afternoon everyone does. People start bringing your boss decisions to sign before your boss can stop being able to sign them.

options.label: Draw the sailboat with the anchors

results.body: You draw the sailboat. The anchors are the things holding the team back. There are a lot of anchors.

title: Wellbeing Hour
narration: A mandatory Wellbeing Hour, in the hour before the deadline. There is a breathing exercise, a slide about burnout, and a reminder that the deadline has not moved.

signs.label: Who leaves early
signs.text: {holder} leaves halfway through, for a call, and nobody minds. {ignored} checks a phone, and is asked to be present.
signs.clue: At the Wellbeing Hour, {holder} left early unremarked, and {ignored} was asked to be present.

signs.label: Who leads the breathing
signs.text: {bystander} breathes in when {holder} does.

options.label: Breathe in for four, and out for four

results.body: You breathe. The deadline does not.

options.label: Point out that the deadline is in an hour

results.body: There is a silence, which the facilitator calls a mindful pause.

options.label: Finish your work on your knee, under the table

results.body: You finish it. The facilitator thanks everyone for being so present.

options.label: Thank your boss for making the time

results.body: Your boss says that wellbeing is a priority, and asks whether the deadline is in hand.

title: Supplier Pitch
narration: A supplier has come to pitch a platform that does what the new tool does, and what the old tool did. There is a free lanyard each.

signs.label: Who the supplier talks to
signs.text: The supplier addresses every slide to {holder}, having asked at reception who decides. {ignored} is handed the brochure.
signs.clue: At the Supplier Pitch, the supplier spoke only to {holder}, and gave {ignored} the brochure.

signs.label: Who asks the price
signs.text: {bystander} asks the price, and looks at {holder} when it is said.

options.label: Ask which of the tools it replaces

results.body: All of them, says the supplier, and none of them, in phase one.

options.label: Ask for a free trial for the whole floor

results.body: The supplier is delighted. The trial is free for thirty days, after which it is not.

options.label: Put on the lanyard

results.body: You put on the lanyard. It says Partner on it.

options.label: Agree with whatever your boss says

results.body: Your boss says it looks interesting. You say it looks very interesting.

title: One Team Day
narration: A day for the whole of Floor 2 to feel like one team. The teams sit at separate tables, by team, and compete.

signs.label: Whose table wins
signs.text: {holder}'s table wins the quiz. Nobody had told the others there was a prize.
signs.clue: At One Team Day, {holder}'s table won the quiz, and only they knew of the prize.

signs.label: Who keeps score
signs.text: {bystander} keeps the score, and checks each total with {holder}.

options.label: Let your team win the quiz

results.body: Your team wins. The prize is a voucher, which is shared, and is for one.

options.label: Suggest mixing the tables

results.body: The tables are mixed. Everyone talks to someone new for ten minutes, and then moves back.

options.label: Offer to keep the score

results.body: You keep the score. It is close, and then it is not.

options.label: Give a short speech about being one team

results.body: Your speech is short, and is applauded by your own table.

title: Budget Planning
narration: Next year's budget is this year's, less ten per cent, plus whatever can be argued for.

signs.label: Whose line survives
signs.text: {holder}'s line stays. {ignored}'s is discussed until it goes.
signs.clue: At Budget Planning, {holder}'s line was kept, and {ignored}'s was discussed until it went.

signs.label: Who holds the spreadsheet
signs.text: {bystander} has the spreadsheet open, and scrolls when {holder} nods.

options.label: Argue for your team's real costs

results.body: You argue. Your line is kept, at ninety per cent, as a compromise with itself.

options.label: Offer to take the ten per cent from your team

results.body: You are thanked for your leadership. Your team is told by the spreadsheet.

options.label: Add twenty per cent to your line, to be cut back

results.body: Your line is cut by ten per cent, and comes out ahead.

options.label: Watch the spreadsheet

results.body: Cells turn red, then amber, then green, then red.

title: Hiring Decision
narration: Your req has been approved: one post, on your team, and the hire is yours. The Senior Analyst has recommended a candidate, and your boss has mentioned one. An old friend of yours is between things, and their CV says transformation eleven times.

signs.label: Whose candidate it is
signs.text: The shortlist goes up. Everyone looks at {holder}, and {holder} looks at nobody.
signs.clue: At the Hiring Decision, everyone looked at {holder} when the shortlist went up.

signs.label: Who is consulted
signs.text: {bystander} is asked for a view, and gives {holder}'s. {ignored} is asked to book the room.

options.label: Hire the Senior Analyst's candidate, who is good

results.body: The candidate starts on Monday, and by Wednesday has found two things wrong with your project. The Senior Analyst is pleased, and tries not to show it.

remembers.text: You hired the candidate they recommended.

options.label: Hire your old friend, who is between things

results.body: Your friend starts on Monday, and on Monday asks what the job is. You tell them. By Friday the Senior Analyst is doing it, and your project has slipped a week.

reaction.believer: Your boss asks to see the scoring sheet. There is no scoring sheet. Your boss writes something down, and underlines it.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss says that a lead needs people they can trust, and asks your friend about golf.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss says that everyone needs their own people, and asks, lightly, how far back the two of you go.

remembers.text: You hired your old friend over the candidate they recommended, and they do your friend's work.

options.label: Hire the candidate your boss mentioned

results.body: Your boss's candidate accepts, and mentions your boss twice in their first week. You are now someone who listens.

options.label: Leave the post empty, and report the saving

results.body: The saving goes upstairs, with a chart. Your team is told that the post has been reimagined, and shares out its work.

title: Pay Review
narration: Your team's bonus pot is twelve thousand pounds, and this year it is yours to divide. Once your boss signs off the split, each share goes out in a letter with your signature on it.

signs.label: Whose split goes through
signs.text: {holder}'s split is signed before it is read. {ignored}'s is read twice.
signs.clue: At the Pay Review, {holder}'s split was signed before anyone read it.

signs.label: Who holds the pen
signs.text: {bystander} passes {holder} the pen, and waits.

options.label: Split it equally across your team

results.body: Every letter has the same sum on it, and you sign each one. By lunchtime your team has compared them, and found nothing to object to, which it holds against you.

options.label: Give it all to whoever really backs you

results.body: You sign two letters for six thousand pounds each, to the Senior Analyst and the Project Co-ordinator, who have been on your side all year. Everyone else on your team gets a letter about the value of recognition.

reaction.believer: Your boss reads the split, and asks what each share was for. You say loyalty. Your boss writes the word down, and looks at it.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss signs the split, and says that loyalty ought to be rewarded, as if it had been.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss signs the split without reading it, and says that people remember who looked after them.

remembers.text: You gave your team's bonus pot to the two who back you, and sent them a letter about recognition.

results.body: You sign one letter, for twelve thousand pounds, to the Senior Analyst, who has been on your side all year. The Project Co-ordinator gets a letter thanking them for their resilience, and reads it twice.

reaction.believer: Your boss reads the split, and asks what each share was for. You say loyalty. Your boss writes the word down, and looks at it.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss signs the split, and says that loyalty ought to be rewarded, as if it had been.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss signs the split without reading it, and says that people remember who looked after them.

remembers.text: You gave your team's whole bonus pot to the Senior Analyst, and sent them a letter about resilience.
You gave your team's bonus pot to one person who backs you, and sent them a letter about resilience.

results.body: You sign one letter, for twelve thousand pounds, to the Project Co-ordinator, who has been on your side all year. The Senior Analyst gets a letter thanking them for their resilience, and files it.

reaction.believer: Your boss reads the split, and asks what each share was for. You say loyalty. Your boss writes the word down, and looks at it.
reaction.incompetent: Your boss signs the split, and says that loyalty ought to be rewarded, as if it had been.
reaction.practitioner: Your boss signs the split without reading it, and says that people remember who looked after them.

results.body: You look down your team for anyone who really backs you, and cannot be sure of one. The pot goes, in one letter, to whoever laughed at your joke on Monday. Everybody else gets a letter about resilience.

reaction.incompetent: Your boss signs the split, and says that loyalty ought to be rewarded, as if it had been.

You gave your team's bonus pot to someone who laughed at your joke, and sent them a letter about resilience.

options.label: Divide it by the year's work, and give the reasons

results.body: The biggest share goes to the Senior Analyst, who did most of the year's work. Each letter gives its reasons, with dates. Your boss asks why your split has an appendix.

remembers.text: You gave them the biggest share of your team's bonus pot, with the reasons in writing.

options.label: Ask your boss how they would split it

results.body: Your boss gives you three names, one of whom is not on your team. You make the sums add up, and sign.

title: Floor Plan Walkthrough
narration: Facilities walks the leads round Floor 2 with a plan and a pencil. Each lead seats their own team: who by whom, who by the window, and who by the lift. The Senior Analyst and the Project Co-ordinator sit together, and talk.

signs.label: Who chooses first
signs.text: {holder} chooses first, and Facilities writes it down at once.
signs.clue: On the Floor Plan Walkthrough, {holder} chose first, and Facilities wrote it down at once.

signs.label: Who gets the lift
signs.text: {ignored}'s team is given the desks by the lift, in passing.

options.label: Leave your team as it sits

results.body: Your team stays where it is. Facilities marks it on the plan as Phase Two, in pencil.

options.label: Split up the Senior Analyst and the Project Co-ordinator

results.body: You put the length of the floor between them. They now talk by e-mail, which is slower, and copy each other in on everything, which is not.

remembers.text: You split them up from the Project Co-ordinator on the floor plan, because they talk.
You split them up from the Senior Analyst on the floor plan, because they talk.

options.label: Put the Project Co-ordinator, who questions your plans, by the lift

results.body: The Project Co-ordinator carries everything to the desk by the lift in one trip, and sets it down beside the fire door. The lift opens, and says Floor 2.

remembers.text: You sat them by the lift, for questioning your plans.

options.label: Take the window yourself, and seat your team facing you

results.body: You have the window. Your team faces you, with the light behind you, and sees only your outline.

title: Succession Planning
narration: Each lead writes down who on their team could step into their job tomorrow. The forms are confidential, and are read out, so each lead hears who would replace them.

signs.label: Whose name comes up
signs.text: {holder}'s name is on two forms that are not {holder}'s own.
signs.clue: At Succession Planning, {holder}'s name was on other leads' forms.

signs.label: Who is on nobody's form
signs.text: {ignored} is on nobody's form, and writes something down.

options.label: Write down the Senior Analyst, who could do it

results.body: The Senior Analyst's name is read out. They look across at you, surprised, and then at your job, with interest.

remembers.text: You named them as the one who could do your job.

options.label: Write that nobody on your team is ready yet

results.body: It is read out. Your team hears that it is not ready, and you hear that you are irreplaceable, which upstairs means something else.

options.label: Write down your old friend

results.body: Your friend's name is read out. There is a short silence, which the Senior Analyst uses.

news.text: You named your old friend as the one who could do your job.

options.label: Write that your old friend has moved on, and go and tell them

results.body: Your friend takes it well, and asks whether they can keep the laptop. They cannot. The leaving drinks are on your card, and you are not invited.

options.label: Write down your boss, as your mentor

results.body: It is read out. Your boss is touched, and points out that they already have a job, which is above yours.

title: Recognition Panel
narration: The leads choose this quarter's Star of the Floor, from every team on Floor 2. There is a certificate and a parking space for a month, and the leads vote.

signs.label: Whose nominee wins
signs.text: {holder}'s nominee has won before the vote. {ignored}'s is noted.
signs.clue: At the Recognition Panel, {holder}'s nominee had won before the vote.

signs.label: Who seconds
signs.text: {bystander} seconds {holder}'s nominee, and then asks who it is.

options.label: Nominate whoever on your team did the most

results.body: You read out what they did. It is a long list, and the leads thank you for its length, and vote for someone else's.

options.label: Vote for the Service Delivery Lead's nominee, for their vote next time

results.body: The Service Delivery Lead's nominee wins by one vote, yours. The Service Delivery Lead nods to you, once, like a receipt.

remembers.text: You voted for their nominee at the Recognition Panel.

options.label: Vote for whoever your boss nominated

results.body: Your boss's nominee wins. Your boss notices who voted for them, which is what the vote was for.

options.label: Second whichever name is said first

results.body: You second it. It was decided already, and now it is unanimous.

title: Org Design Workshop
narration: The leads redraw the floor's boxes on a whiteboard. Lines may be moved and boxes merged. Nobody in a box is to be told until the boxes are final.

signs.label: Who holds the pen
signs.text: {holder} holds the pen, and the boxes move towards {holder}.
signs.clue: At the Org Design Workshop, {holder} held the pen, and the boxes moved towards them.

signs.label: Whose box goes
signs.text: {ignored}'s box is merged into a box called Shared Services, which is drawn larger.

options.label: Keep your box the shape it is

results.body: Your box stays the same shape. Someone draws a dotted line to it, and will not say from where.

options.label: Draw another team's line into your box

results.body: Your box is bigger. It has a team in it now that has not been told, and a lead who has.

options.label: Draw the Project Co-ordinator's line into someone else's box

results.body: The line is moved. The Project Co-ordinator is now in Shared Services, on the whiteboard, until somebody wipes it.

remembers.text: You drew their line out of your team at the Org Design Workshop.

options.label: Ask for a week, so as to ask your team

results.body: You are given a week, and the boxes are finalised in the meantime.

title: Ways of Working Charter
narration: The leads agree a charter for how Floor 2 works: core hours, time without meetings, and the tone of e-mails. Once agreed, it will be laminated.

signs.label: Whose hours are core
signs.text: {holder}'s working hours become the floor's core hours, without a vote.
signs.clue: At the Ways of Working Charter, {holder}'s hours became the core hours without a vote.

signs.label: Who laminates
signs.text: {ignored} is asked to laminate it.

options.label: Propose core hours that suit your team

results.body: Your team's hours are noted, and the core hours are set at the hours already set.

options.label: Propose Fridays without meetings

results.body: Fridays without meetings are agreed, and a meeting is booked on each one, to protect it.

options.label: Propose adopting the Programme Office's charter

results.body: It is adopted. It turns out to be last year's, with this year's date on it.

options.label: Say nothing, and sign it

results.body: You sign it. The charter is laminated, and goes on the wall beside the last one.

title: Cost Challenge
narration: Your first week as a Middle manager, and the Chief Financial Officer wants thirty per cent off every budget on Floor 3, with everything in the plan still delivered. The Chief Financial Officer has joined by phone, from a car, to say that this is not a cut but a challenge.

signs.label: Whose budget is challenged first
signs.text: {ignored}'s budget is challenged first, and hardest. {holder}'s is challenged last, and briefly.
signs.clue: At the Cost Challenge, {holder}'s budget was challenged last, and briefly.

signs.label: Who rings back
signs.text: When the line drops, {bystander} rings the car back, and hands the phone to {holder}.

options.label: Make the cut, and ask in writing what will stop because of it

results.body: Your list of what will stop is two pages long, and the first line is the Roadmap's. The Chief Financial Officer says that it is very helpful, and that the plan has not changed. The list is filed with the plan, behind it.

options.label: Cut the testing and the second checks, which nobody sees

results.body: It comes to thirty per cent exactly, and nothing in the plan moves. The Service Delivery Lead reads what has gone, and asks who will check things now. You say that everyone will, a bit.

remembers.text: You cut the checks they run, to meet the thirty per cent, and kept the plan as it was.

options.label: Pass the cut down to your team, and keep the plan

results.body: Each of your team is asked to find thirty per cent of their own, by Friday. The Senior Analyst loses a contractor and the Project Co-ordinator a training course, and both are told that it is a challenge.

remembers.text: You passed the Chief Financial Officer's cut down to them, and they lost their contractor.
You passed the Chief Financial Officer's cut down to them, and they lost their training.

options.label: Move a third of your costs onto Floor 2's codes

results.body: A third of your costs go downstairs, to codes on Floor 2 that nobody on Floor 3 owns. Floor 3's budget is thirty per cent lower. The company's is the same.

title: The Board Offsite
location: A hotel with a lake, the Orangery
narration: The Board's offsite, in an orangery with no oranges. Your boss has the morning. Floor 3 has the two hours after lunch, which overran, so they are now an hour and three quarters.

signs.label: Whom the Board turns to
signs.text: Whenever a slide changes, the Board turns to {holder}, to see what to think of it.
signs.clue: At the Board Offsite, the Board turned to {holder} whenever a slide changed.

signs.label: Who is not offered a pastry
signs.text: {ignored} is the only one not offered a pastry, and says they did not want one.

options.label: Present the plan as it is, and stop when it runs out

results.body: It runs to the minute, because you wrote it to. The Board asks four questions, all of them about the plan, which nobody on Floor 3 can remember happening before. Your boss's boss eats the pastry.
It is very good, and you are seeing most of it for the first time. The Board asks who wrote slide forty. You say your team, and the Board writes down your team.
It is last year's plan, and runs to the minute, as it did last year. Some of the Board remember it, and are too polite to say so in the room.
It is One Roadmap, on one slide, with everything on it. You talk to it for as long as the Board can look at it, which is twenty minutes, and the Board says that it can see the shape of it.
It runs out after forty minutes. The Board takes an early coffee, and thanks you for the time back, which it says is the most useful thing anyone has given it all day.

options.label: Fill the two hours, whatever it takes

results.body: There is a breakout, a live poll and an exercise with a beach ball, which ends up in the lake. The two hours are filled. Nobody can say afterwards with what, and everyone says it was energising.

options.label: Present it as your own work, and take the applause

results.body: You present your team's night as your own vision. The Board applauds. The Junior Associate, who wrote slide forty, is in the car park, waiting to drive the deck back.

remembers.text: You presented the deck they wrote overnight to the Board as your own.

results.body: You present it as your own vision, which it is, in that nobody else will put their name to it. The Board applauds the vision, and asks for the detail by Monday.

options.label: Use the two hours to have the Board decide what stops

results.body: It takes both hours. Two programmes are stopped, out loud, and their owners take it badly and then, by the coffee, with relief. {plan} is shorter, and true.

options.label: Show {plan} as swimlanes, with everything on it and no dates

results.body: Everything is on it, nothing is stopped, and nothing has a date, so nothing is late. It is the best-looking slide of the offsite, and the Board photographs it.

title: The Board
location: Floor 3, Steering Room 3A, with the Board on the screen
narration: Floor 3's fifteen minutes at the Board. The Board is on the screen, in a room with better chairs. You are on slide nine of twelve when {competitor} asks, warmly, why the figure on slide seven is lower than last year's.

competitor.title: A particularly tricky question, at the Board
competitor.label: How the question is asked

signs.text: {competitor} asks it as a favour to the Board, and has slide seven open already.
{competitor} asks it as if it had only just occurred to them, and seems surprised by it.
{competitor} asks it apologetically, and says that somebody had to.

signs.label: Whom the screen watches
signs.text: While the question hangs there, the Board watches {holder}, to see how to take it.
signs.clue: At the Board, the screen watched {holder} while the question about slide seven hung there.

options.label: Say that you do not know yet, and when you will

results.body: You do know, as it turns out, because you checked every figure in the pack on Friday. You say it once. The Board moves on to lunch, and {competitor} closes slide seven.
You say that you do not have it to hand, and that the Board will have it by Friday. The Board writes Friday down. So does {competitor}, in a different colour.

options.label: Give a figure that sounds about right

results.body: You say eleven per cent, firmly, and the Board nods. The Office Co-ordinator, who is taking the minutes, writes eleven per cent down. The Senior Analyst, who knows the figure, looks at the table.

options.label: Say that it is a great question, and take it offline

results.body: You say that it is a great question. The Board agrees that it is, and would like the answer offline, in writing, before the next Board. {competitor} offers to help, and is thanked.

options.label: Say that the figure came from the Senior Analyst

results.body: You say it. By the afternoon the recording of the Board has gone upstairs, and come back down with a question about you on it, from someone on a floor that is closed.
results.factNote: At the Board, you put a figure down to the Senior Analyst. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: You say it. The Board writes down the Senior Analyst's name, and the Senior Analyst, at the end of the table, writes down yours.

remembers.text: You put your figure down to them, in front of the Board.

options.label: Ask {competitor} the same about their own figures

results.body: You ask it warmly, as a favour to the Board. {competitor} does not have their own figures open, and says so, at length. The Board minutes it as healthy challenge.

title: Stakeholder Mapping
narration: Everyone puts everyone else on a grid of power against interest. It is anonymous, and done on a whiteboard, in front of everyone.

signs.label: Who is put top right
signs.text: Four pens in four colours put {holder} in the top right corner. Nobody puts themselves there.
signs.clue: At Stakeholder Mapping, everyone put {holder} in the top right corner.

signs.label: Who is left off
signs.text: {ignored} is not on the grid at all, and notices, and says it is fine.

options.label: Put people where you have seen them act, not by title

results.body: Your pen moves two people away from their job titles. One of them sees, and looks at the grid for a long time, and then at you.

options.label: Put your boss's boss in the top right, large

results.body: You draw your boss's boss in the top right, larger than the corner. Your boss's boss pretends not to have seen it, and has it photographed.

options.label: Put the Senior Analyst in the bottom left, and say why

results.body: You say why. By the afternoon the photograph of the grid has gone upstairs, and come back down with a question about you on it, from someone on a floor that is closed.
results.factNote: You put the Senior Analyst at the bottom of Floor 3's grid, out loud. You had not been told why that was a mistake.

results.body: You say why. The Senior Analyst is not in the room, and hears about it before the meeting ends, from three people, each of whom says they were not going to mention it.

remembers.text: You put them at the bottom of the grid on Floor 3, and said why.

options.label: Say that you are still new, and pass the pen

results.body: You pass the pen. It is taken by the person who most wanted it, which tells you more than the grid does.

title: Portfolio Review
narration: A Portfolio Review, with a slide of a road. The road has no cars on it, and goes over a hill, and everything Floor 3 is doing is somewhere on it.

signs.label: Whom the slides face
signs.text: The projector is angled at {holder}, and so is everyone's chair.
signs.clue: At a Portfolio Review, the projector and the chairs were angled at {holder}.

signs.label: Whose programme is skipped
signs.text: {ignored}'s programme is on slide nine, and the meeting ends on slide eight.

options.label: Ask what the portfolio will stop

results.body: There is a pause, of the kind that gets minuted. Your boss says that nothing needs to stop, because everything is aligned. Your question is written on the whiteboard, and photographed.

options.label: Say that the vision is bold

results.body: You say it. Your boss says that bold is the point. Three other people say bold, in turn, more boldly.

options.label: Volunteer to own the portfolio

results.body: You volunteer. Your boss thanks you for stepping up, and steps back, a long way.

options.label: Read your e-mail under the table

results.body: Forty e-mails, all of which say they are following up. You follow up on none of them, which is what Floor 3 calls prioritising.

title: Steering Group
narration: The Steering Group, which meets to steer. The minutes of the last one are approved, and nobody can remember what was steered.

signs.label: Who approves the minutes
signs.text: The minutes are approved when {holder} nods. Nobody had asked for a nod.
signs.clue: At a Steering Group, the minutes were approved when {holder} nodded.

signs.label: Whose action is carried forward
signs.text: {ignored}'s action is carried forward again, for the fourth meeting running.

options.label: Raise a risk that is actually happening

results.body: You raise it. It is noted, given an owner, who is you, and a rating, which is amber, because red would need a meeting.

options.label: Propose stopping one programme, so the Roadmap is true

results.body: You propose it. There is a long silence and then a vote, which nobody has held here before. The programme stops. The Roadmap has one fewer line and one more date.

options.label: Add a swimlane for everything not on the Roadmap yet

results.body: The new swimlane is called Emerging. Everything goes into it, and the Roadmap is now complete, in the sense of having everything on it.

options.label: Agree with whoever is chairing

results.body: You agree. The chair agrees with you agreeing, and the meeting ends early, which is minuted as an achievement.

title: Benefits Realisation Review
narration: A review of the benefits last year's programmes said they would realise. They are in a spreadsheet, in a folder called Archive.

signs.label: Whose benefits are counted
signs.text: {holder}'s benefits are counted first, and generously, by {bystander}.
signs.clue: At the Benefits Realisation Review, {holder}'s benefits were counted first, and generously.

signs.label: Whose spreadsheet is opened
signs.text: {ignored}'s spreadsheet is opened, and closed again, before anyone reads it.

options.label: Count your team's benefits properly, missing ones included

results.body: Your benefits come to about a third of what was promised. It is the only honest number in the review, and it is circled.

options.label: Count the same saving under two programmes

results.body: The saving appears twice, once under each name. The total goes up. Nobody adds it up the other way.

options.label: Tie each benefit to a Roadmap line, and drop lines with none

results.body: You tie each benefit to a line. Three lines have none, and you drop them. The Roadmap is shorter, and for the first time it says what it is for.

options.label: Praise the benefits framework

results.body: You praise the framework. Its author is in the room, and thanks you, and will remember you, in a meeting you are not in.

title: Lessons Learned Forum
narration: A forum for the lessons Floor 3 has learned. They are the same lessons as last year's, on a newer template.

signs.label: Whose lesson it is
signs.text: Every lesson names someone who has left. {holder} chose the template.
signs.clue: At the Lessons Learned Forum, {holder} had chosen the template.

signs.label: Who is asked to present
signs.text: {ignored} is asked to present the lessons, and none of them are {ignored}'s.

options.label: Offer a lesson that is your own fault

results.body: You offer one. The room is very quiet, and then very supportive, which on Floor 3 is the same thing said later.

options.label: Put your lesson down to someone who has left

results.body: The lesson goes to someone who has left, who cannot attend to accept it. It is accepted on their behalf.

options.label: Present the Roadmap as a lesson already learned

results.body: You present the Roadmap as what Floor 3 has learned. It has no dates, which you call agility. It is applauded, and filed under Done.

options.label: Offer to take the notes

results.body: You take the notes. They are the only record of the forum, so you decide what was learned.

title: Roadmap Workshop
narration: A workshop on what Floor 3 is doing, with sticky notes in four colours. Everyone was asked to leave their job title at the door. Nobody has.

signs.label: Whose notes stay up
signs.text: {holder}'s sticky notes stay up. Everyone else's are moved, gently, to a column called Later.
signs.clue: At the Roadmap Workshop, {holder}'s sticky notes were the only ones not moved to Later.

signs.label: Who gets the facilitator
signs.text: The facilitator asks {bystander} what {holder} thinks, and writes the answer down.

options.label: Ask the Senior Analyst what is really running

results.body: The Senior Analyst has a list. It is longer than the Roadmap, and includes the Roadmap.

options.label: Get the room to decide what stops

results.body: It takes the whole afternoon. Two programmes are stopped, out loud, and their owners take it badly and then, by six o'clock, with relief. The Roadmap is shorter, and true.

options.label: Turn the notes into swimlanes, with no dates

results.body: You photograph the wall and turn it into swimlanes, in the company colours. Everything is on it, nothing is stopped, and nothing has a date. It is the best-looking thing on Floor 3.

options.label: Move your own sticky note into Now

results.body: Your note goes into Now. Nobody stops you, and nobody will be able to say later that they did.

title: Reforecast
narration: The year's forecast, again. It was forecast in January and reforecast in April, and is now being re-reforecast, because the Chief Financial Officer did not like April.

signs.label: Whose number becomes the forecast
signs.text: {holder}'s number becomes the forecast. Everyone else's becomes a range.
signs.clue: At a Reforecast, {holder}'s number became the forecast, and everyone else's a range.

signs.label: Who explains a difference
signs.text: {ignored} is asked to explain a difference, which turns out to be the gap between what {ignored} said and what {holder} wanted.

options.label: Forecast what you actually expect

results.body: You forecast what you expect, which is lower. The room goes quiet. The forecast then goes up anyway, by someone else's pen, and yours is kept as a footnote.

options.label: Forecast low, so that you can beat it later

results.body: You forecast low. Next quarter you will beat it, and be thanked for the surprise, which you have scheduled.

options.label: Forecast whatever your boss forecast

results.body: Your forecast matches your boss's to the pound. Your boss calls it alignment. The Chief Financial Officer's office calls it a coincidence, and asks for the workings.

options.label: Ask how the forecast is actually worked out

results.body: Nobody knows. There is a spreadsheet with a tab called DO NOT TOUCH, and someone touched it four years ago, and left.

title: Board Rehearsal
narration: A rehearsal for the next Board. Your boss's boss plays the Board, and is better at it than the Board is.

signs.label: Who plays the Chair
signs.text: {holder} is given the Chair's seat for the rehearsal, and is still in it when the rehearsal ends.
signs.clue: At a Board Rehearsal, {holder} was given the Chair's seat, and kept it.

signs.label: Whose slides are cut for time
signs.text: {ignored}'s slides are cut for time before anyone has seen them, including {ignored}.

options.label: Ask to be asked the hardest question there is

results.body: You are asked it, and get it wrong, here, where it does not count. That is what a rehearsal is for, and nobody in the room believes it.

options.label: Agree a friendly question for the day with your boss's boss

results.body: Your boss's boss agrees to ask you something easy on the day, and asks what you will do in return. You say anything. Your boss's boss writes anything down.

options.label: Cut your section to one slide, with a photograph

results.body: Your section is one slide: a photograph of a bridge. It is the only slide the rehearsal remembers, and nobody can say what it was about.

options.label: Offer to keep time

results.body: You keep time. Everyone overruns except the one person you would have expected to, which you note.

title: Team Structure Review
narration: Floor 3 is reviewing how many people report to how many people. The answer is going to be fewer, and the question is who.

signs.label: Whose chart is not redrawn
signs.text: Every chart on the wall is redrawn, except {holder}'s, which is admired.
signs.clue: At the Team Structure Review, {holder}'s chart was the only one not redrawn.

signs.label: Who is drawn as a dotted line
signs.text: {ignored} ends the meeting as a dotted line, and is told that dotted lines are very important.

options.label: Say what each of your team does, and that you need all of them

results.body: You go through your team one by one, with what each of them actually does. It takes twenty minutes, and the room is surprised by how much of it there is.

options.label: Offer up the post you have never been able to fill

results.body: You offer up the post that has been empty for a year. It is counted as a saving, a reduction and a difficult decision, bravely taken.

options.label: Say that Floor 3 has too many layers, starting below you

results.body: Your boss agrees that there are too many layers, and that the ones below are the place to start. Nobody below is in the room.

options.label: Offer to draw the new chart

results.body: You draw it. Where to put the lines turns out to be most of the decision, and nobody has noticed that yet.
